items.title: #DataViz: Where does India shut down the internet?
items.summary: India saw more than 900 internet shutdowns in 15 years, which translates to a shutdown order every six days, on average, according to our analysis of data compiled by the Software Freedom Law Center (SFLC). Two in three of these were in Jammu and Kashmir, Rajasthan and Manipur. Preventive shutdowns, imposed in anticipation of an event, accounted for 70% (654) recorded incidents, while the rest were categorised as ‘reactive’. The longest shutdown in the tracker lasted 552 days in Jammu and Kashmir, where internet access was restricted from August 4, 2019, after the abrogation of Article 370, until 4G services were restored on February 6, 2021. Manipur’s statewide shutdown, imposed after violence broke out in May 2023, lasted 200 days. Recorded shutdowns fell from a peak of 136 in 2018 to 33 so far in 2026. Delhi recorded 11 internet shutdowns in 15 years, seven of them in 2026—as many as in Manipur and more than in any other state or Union territory this year. Globally, India had the most internet shutdowns of any country since 2019, according to the Internet Society’s Pulse shutdown tracker . Iraq had the second highest, followed by Syria and Sudan. items.title: Supreme Court upholds NCLAT order to reconsider Videocon resolution plan involving over 95% haircut
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed the appeals against the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal’s (NCLAT) decision to send Twinstar Technologies’ ₹2,962 crore resolution plan for 13 Videocon group companies back to creditors for reconsideration. The plan involved a haircut exceeding 95 percent for creditors. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe also affirmed the NCLAT’s power to return an approved resolution plan to the Committee of Creditors (CoC) and laid down guidelines governing the exercise of that power. “We have upheld the power of the NCLAT to send the approved resolution plan to the CoC. And for the reasons assigned by us, we have dismissed all the appeals,” the Court said while pronouncing its verdict. A detailed copy of the judgment is awaited. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The case arose from Twinstar Technologies’ proposal to take over 13 Videocon group companies through the insolvency resolution process. The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) at Mumbai approved the ₹2,962 crore resolution plan on June 8, 2021. This was against the admitted liabilities of around ₹65,000 crore which meant the plan involved a haircut exceeding 95 percent. In other words, creditors would stand to lose nearly ₹62,000 crore. The plan received approval from lenders holding 95.09 percent of the Committee of Creditors’ (CoC) voting share. Three lenders, Bank of Maharashtra, IFCI and SIDBI, challenged the approval before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT). The dissenting lenders questioned the amounts allocated to them and the proposal to pay through non-convertible debentures redeemable after approximately five years. The appellate tribunal noted discrepancies between the amounts recorded in the resolution professional’s compliance certificate and the distribution calculations shared by SBI Caps. It also held that dissenting creditors could not be compelled to accept securities in place of the monetary payment required under the Code. items.title: RISE Legal India: 300 lawyers to gather in Mumbai as RSGI reveals its 2026 Resight India Law Firm Ratings
items.summary: London-based legal research and advisory firm RSGI will unveil its RISE Law Firm Ratings 2026 at the RISE Legal India conference, scheduled for November 18 at The St Regis, Mumbai. After 18 years of rating India's law firms, RSGI is asking a harder question: not just who wins the work, but who is built for what comes next. The 2026 RISE Law Firm Ratings judge Indian firms and international India practices on AI, pricing, management and talent, drawing on submissions, managing partner interviews and client feedback. According to RSGI, 85 Indian law firms submitted information for the assessment, while 36 international firms' India practices were evaluated. The exercise involved 101 interviews with managing partners and India practice heads, along with more than 650 client references. The conference, titled Evolutions in the Practice of Law , is expected to bring together around 300 delegates, including law firm partners, general counsel and legal technology executives. The opening session on reforming India's legal industry will feature former Bombay High Court judge Justice Gautam Patel , Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas Managing Partner Cyril Shroff , Boeing's Akhil Prasad and Hogan Lovells Cadwalader's Ajay Kuntamukkala . A discussion on changing priorities and pricing strategies among general counsel will feature Nilanjan Sinha (ICICI Bank), Sapan Gupta (ArcelorMittal), Pooja Bedi (Hindustan Coca-Cola), Madhav Uppuluri (TCS); moderated by Yasmin Lambert, RSGI. Another session on transforming legal businesses will feature Khaitan & Co's Haigreve Khaitan , iManage's Neil Araujo , Harvey's Pratik Joshi , PwC UK's Sandeep Agrawal and Aditya Birla Group's Deepak Acharya . The conference will also examine whether artificial intelligence can exercise legal judgement, with AZB & Partners' Zia Mody, Trilegal's Rahul Matthan, National Law School of India University Vice-Chancellor Sudhir Krishnaswamy and Fairsight's Espen Skorstad participating. Interactive workshops will focus on dispute resolution, deal-making, cross-border legal work and AI adoption. A competition organised by Khaitan & Co with technology partner Leah will allow lawyers to develop AI-powered workflows to address practical legal problems. RSGI, which has assessed India's legal market since 2008, will announce the ratings at the conference's conclusion. items.title: After Arnab and Murasu, third cyclone ‘Akvan’ to hit Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm, named Akvan, by the evening of November 16 and further strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. The system is moving north-northwestwards over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal. It is expected to gather strength over the next two days and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. This would be the third cyclone to affect Andhra Pradesh in the past few weeks after Cyclones Arnab and Murasu caused extensive damage. The weather system intensified into a deep depression on November 15, when it was located about 640 km east-northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 760 km east-southeast of Chennai and 870 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam. Andhra Pradesh is also awaiting a central assessment of the damage caused by Cyclone Murasu and the subsequent financial aid from the BJP led Union government. Cyclone Murasu struck the state earlier this month. A seven-member central team led by Union Home Ministry Joint Secretary Chittaranjan Das has completed field inspections across Bapatla, Palnadu, Eluru and East Godavari districts. The team examined nearly 60 locations in two groups, assessing damage to crops, roads, drainage systems, houses, irrigation infrastructure and fishing boats. During the inspections, officials interacted with farmers at Surappagudem in Bhimadole mandal, examined paddy fields and drainage facilities at Ravulapalem, and assessed damage to the Kommu canal and irrigation infrastructure at Kunakalamarri. Fishing boats at Chirala and houses and horticultural crops at Boppudi were also inspected. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has urged the team to submit its assessment report within 10 days. According to the state government's estimates, Cyclone Murasu caused losses of Rs 2,484.43 crore. Roads and related infrastructure accounted for Rs 888.84 crore, while crop damage across 1,43,617 hectares was estimated at Rs 874.97 crore, affecting 1,86,063 farmers. East Godavari reportedly suffered more rainfall-related damage than during Cyclone Arnab. Paddy losses were estimated at 80% in East Godavari and up to 90% in Eluru, with mango and papaya among the worst-hit horticultural crops.

items.title: Teen dies by electrocution: Kerala Electricity Board issues apology, orders investigation
items.summary: The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) issued a public apology on Sunday, November 15 following the tragic death by electrocution of 14-year-old Junaid in Tirurangadi of Malappuram district. In the apology note, KSEB formally admitted official negligence, offered an apology to the family and ordered a detailed inquiry headed by a Chief Engineer. “The death of 14-year-old Junaid, who was electrocuted by the stay wire of an electric pole in Tirurangadi, Malappuram, is deeply heartbreaking. What happened should never have happened. We sincerely apologise to the public,” KSEB’s apology note read. Junaid was a native of Cherumukku Padinjarethara in Tirurangadi. On Sunday morning, he went to a paddy field near his house with friends to fish and watch a tractor plough the land. He touched a broken stay wire attached to an electricity pole that had come into contact with a live overhead power line. Junaid’s friends attempted to pull him away, but a nearby tractor driver intervened and stopped them from touching the live wire, saving them from a similar incident. Junaid was given CPR and rushed to a nearby hospital; however, he could not be saved. The incident sparked widespread local protests and demands for accountability from youth organisations such as the Youth League and the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI). In the apology note, KSEB promised to conduct an impartial, thorough investigation under the leadership of the Deputy Chief Engineer of the Tirur Electrical Circle and strict action against those found responsible. KSEB also said it would ensure such incidents do not happen again. “The safety of the general public and our employees is of paramount importance to KSEB. We will take effective measures to ensure that such accidents do not happen again.” It also instructed patrols of all electrical lines, identification of potential hazards and their elimination. “We request our valued consumers to help prevent such accidents. If you notice any electrical hazard, please share photographs and relevant details via WhatsApp at 9496010101.

items.title: Kallakurichi MLA row: NCW seeks inquiry by TN DGP, cites TNM report
items.summary: The National Commission for Women (NCW) has sought an impartial inquiry by the Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police (DGP) into allegations that TVK MLA C Arul Vignesh, who represents Kallakurichi, sent obscene WhatsApp messages to District Collector JE Padmaja. The Commission has also sought a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR) within seven days. The NCW took suo motu cognisance of a news report published by The News Minute on November 11, on the allegations against the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) legislator. In a statement shared on social media, the Commission said, "The chairperson, Vijaya Rahatkar, had written to the Tamil Nadu DGP, seeking a fair and impartial enquiry into the allegations, including examination of the representations reportedly made by the Collector to senior officials and the action taken on them." The Commission has also called for the preservation and examination of relevant digital evidence, stressing that the investigation should be conducted without political or external influence, irrespective of the position held by the person concerned. “The dignity, safety and security of women public officials must be upheld without exception. No position or influence can place anyone above accountability for alleged harassment or misconduct,” the NCW said. items.title: TN govt suspends five library officials over AI book scam
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government suspended five senior officials of the Directorate of Public Libraries, on Sunday, November 15, over alleged large-scale irregularities in the procurement of books for government libraries across the state. The alleged irregularities include the purchase of AI-generated publications, books containing fabricated information, fictitious author names and titles carrying questionable International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs). The suspensions were ordered by School Education Minister A Rajmohan, four days after the Madras High Court directed the state government to initiate disciplinary proceedings against officials allegedly involved in the irregularities and ordered the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) to register an FIR. The suspended officials include S Kamatchi, Chief Librarian and Information Officer (in-charge) and Deputy Chief Librarian at Anna Centenary Library (ACL), Chennai; Dinesh Kumar, Chief Librarian and Information Officer (in-charge) at Kalaignar Centenary Library (KCL), Madurai; V Santhanakrishnan, Librarian and Information Officer at KCL, who also held additional charge of Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore; S Santhana Karthikeyan, Librarian and Information Officer at ACL; and J Juliet, Chief Accounts Officer of the Directorate of Public Libraries. The Chief Accounts Officer and the Chief Librarian of ACL were also members of the Book Procurement Negotiation Committee, which was responsible for negotiating prices with publishers. The suspensions follow an internal inquiry into the alleged procurement irregularities. However, the department has not made public the inquiry order or its findings. The controversy first came to light after writer Perumal Murugan flagged alleged inaccuracies and fabricated historical and literary references in books stocked at the newly inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore. Perumal Murugan identified nearly 1,800 allegedly dubious books bearing the imprint of Agal Vilakku Pathippagam and more than 100 books published by Phoenix 2023 at the library. He raised concerns over fictitious authors, questionable historical claims, factual inaccuracies and the possibility of AI-generated content. items.title: Another minor files complaint, ninth POCSO case registered against Veeramani
items.summary: The Greater Chennai Police (GCP) have registered a ninth case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against Gem Granites chairman R Veeramani following a fresh complaint by another minor girl alleging sexual abuse. According to the police, the fresh case was registered on November 13 based on the statement of the survivor. The police have also arrested Perumal alias Bala, a former driver of Veeramani, for allegedly bringing minor girls to him and facilitating the offences. He was arrested on Saturday, November 14, and remanded to judicial custody at the Puzhal Central Prison. With the latest case, nine POCSO cases have been registered against Veeramani, involving 13 minor girls. Ten people, including Veeramani, have been arrested in connection with the cases. Separately, Veeramani was booked in 2004 for allegedly abetting the suicide of a minor girl. A chargesheet was filed on November 11 in one of the nine POCSO cases, with the trial set to commence. The case also names former Chennai Police Commissioner Arun as an accused. Meanwhile, the SIT on Saturday conducted a search at Veeramani's residence in Royapettah, Chennai, following a survivor's statement before a special court that the body of a minor girl had been buried on the premises. The search was conducted in the presence of the Mylapore tahsildar and an executive magistrate. The police brought in an excavator and dug up a portion of the premises where a swimming pool was located. However, after nearly six hours of excavation, the SIT called off the search without finding any remains. Veeramani was arrested on August 29 by the Greater Chennai Police's Anti-Vice Squad, along with Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan. He is currently lodged at Puzhal Central Prison. Veeramani's former employee Ganesan, who allegedly possessed another video related to the case but did not inform the police, was arrested on September 22. Three drivers — Lazar, Parthiban and Babu — were arrested on October 5 for allegedly facilitating the offences by bringing minor girls to Veeramani. Sakthivel, a manager at Gem Granites, was arrested on October 18 for allegedly assisting Veeramani. Seenu alias Srinivasan, a security guard at Veeramani's residence, was also arrested for allegedly failing to alert the authorities despite being aware that minor girls were being brought to the house.

items.title: Keralam: Muslims step in to help with two Hindu women's final rites
items.summary: Since childhood, Kalyani Amma has been simply "Amma" to Razak, now a 51-year-old. "She is not 'like my mother'; she is my mother," he says. It's a feeling shared by his younger brother Sulaiman. On November 7, when the 86-year-old died in Vaduvanchal, Wayanad, she had no children or living relatives. Razak and Sulaiman performed her last rites according to Hindu rites. Some 115 km away in Pallikkara, Malappuram, the Khadeeja mosque opened its doors for the last rites of another Hindu woman on November 10. Premalatha, 52, lived in a rented house too small for her body to be bathed and prepared for the final rites. The mosque offered its grounds instead. Both the incidents became headlines but it wasn't anything unusual for the people who were involved in it. For them, living together peacefully and offering support to neighbors is simply a normal way of life, rather than an extraordinary deed deserving public attention. ‘She is my mother’ Kalyani Amma worked multiple jobs to make a living; she had a cattle and used to do cleaning work at a private bank. But for the last 25 years, she has not worked, and Razak has been taking care of her. “When she had cattle, I used to help her sell the milk in my childhood. When she became old, I took care of her,” Razak said. Razak said his family consistently celebrated festivals like Onam and Vishu alongside Kalyani Amma. “Even after my children got married and moved to distant places, returning home to celebrate every festival with Amma was an absolute necessity for them,” he said. Razak’s wife, Rukia, who was with Kalyani Amma at the time of death, said, “She gave me the wedding dress for my marriage. Since then, she has also been my Amma,” she added. Kalyani Amma was admitted to a private hospital on November 6 and died the next day. A few days before her death, Kalyani Amma asked Razak and Sulaiman to perform her last rites, as she also considered them her children. “That’s what Amma said to us in her last days. So we did it. She only has us,” Razak said.
